- If sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast lows by 2–5%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +5% from prior day), model frequently overcorrects; cap next-day forecast at 10% below peak.
- When sentiment swings sharply (e.g., 0.33 → 1.00 or vice versa), model reacts too slowly; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to align with sentiment shift.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 75→70→72), model often holds trend; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in subsequent days.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the period; apply downward bias of 1–3% on first 7–10 days if sentiment is neutral or bearish.
- If sentiment history includes multiple 0.00 or negative values, model underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast for next 3–5 days.
